findings.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser drops the per-user filter `filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` that the old code applied, so user-search authorization now relies solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, which is left unset whenever getGroupIdsWithViewPermission returns an empty set. A caller with no view-users role and no group view-members permissions (or a cross-realm admin, or any case where the granted-group set is empty) previously got zero results because every UserModel failed canView(); now the stream is returned unfiltered, leaking users who are not members of any group, and getUsersCount (still group-filtered, lines 395-425) disagrees with the search results for the same caller.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage when the caller holds only the VIEW scope on all-groups (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), diverging from the interface contract that canManage requires a MANAGE permission. An admin granted only view permission over all groups can create, update and delete groups (GroupsResource gates create/update on canManage()), an unintended privilege escalation relative to the V1 semantics and the documented contract in GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage().

[ADVISORY] The new test class covers VIEW_MEMBERS, MANAGE_MEMBERS and MANAGE scopes but contains no test for the MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP scope added to the Groups resource type, and no test that a user who is not a member of any permitted group stays hidden from search after the per-user filter removal. A regression in manage-membership authorization (canManageMembership in GroupPermissionsV2/UserPermissionsV2 canManageByGroup path) or in the ungrouped-user leak would pass CI unnoticed; the ungrouped-user case is exactly the edge case the filter removal in UsersResource.java:445-453 changes.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission falls back to the all-groups resource whenever a per-group resource is not found, evaluating the all-groups policy's scopes for a specific group request, and this fallback path (including the policyStore.findByResource isEmpty guard) has no dedicated test in the diff. The commented 'fallback to all-groups permission' behavior exercised only incidentally via testManageAllGroups; a regression in the isEmpty guard (e.g., returning the type-resource's scopes when no all-groups permission exists) would silently grant group-level access to any caller when a single type-resource resource exists without policies.

[ADVISORY] GroupPermissions.canList() was changed from canView()-first to QUERY_GROUPS-first and canManage()/canView() changed from users().canManageDefault()/canViewDefault() to direct role checks, while V1's getGroupsWithViewPermission lost its canManage() shortcut (now only root.users().canView()) — several subtle authorization-behavior changes bundled without any V1-path test updates in the visible diff. Existing fine-grained-authz deployments on the V1 path get silently altered evaluation order and manage-only admin behavior (e.g., a manage-users-only admin querying group lists now depends on canView() semantics that changed) with no regression coverage pinning the old contract.

[ADVISORY] The public static utility ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes is deleted while the diff only redirects its single in-tree caller, leaving any out-of-tree caller of the spi-private API with a compile break instead of a deprecation. Downstream extensions calling ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes fail to compile against this change; a @Deprecated forwarding stub would have preserved the public surface.

[BUG] The diff removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter from searchForUser (and the equivalent structure in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser), replacing an in-stream authorization filter with only the UserModel.GROUPS session-attribute restriction — a behavior change not traceable to 'add Groups resource type and scopes'. When getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set for a caller who lacks global view but the underlying user storage provider ignores the session attribute (e.g. federated/custom UserQueryProvider implementations that do not honor UserModel.GROUPS), unauthorized users are returned where the previous code guaranteed filtering; also callers with canView()==true but restricted group visibility via fine-grained user permissions lose the per-user canView check entirely.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller holds only a VIEW permission on all-groups, because it evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). An admin granted only view-groups can create groups and perform manage-scope operations (e.g. GroupsResource.add, which requires canManage), a privilege escalation inconsistent with canManage(group) which correctly requires only MANAGE.

[BUG] The V1 GroupPermissions.canManage()/canView() were rewritten from `root.users().canManageDefault()/canViewDefault()` to direct hasOneAdminRole checks, dropping the indirect dependency on fine-grained user permissions that users().canView()/canManage() previously included. In the V1 (non-V2) path, a caller who previously satisfied group view/manage via fine-grained user-level permissions (users().canView() includes the view-users authorization permission, not just admin roles) now loses group visibility — a silent permission regression unrelated to the stated goal of adding the Groups resource type.

[ADVISORY] The rewrite of ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse to try-with-resources is unrelated refactoring bundled into a PR whose stated intent is adding the Groups resource type and scopes. Reviewers and bisect operate on a mixed-intent diff; if the response-close change regresses (e.g. getResponse read-after-close), it will be attributed to the authz change.

[ADVISORY] The public utility ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes is deleted outright rather than deprecated, removing a public API surface as a side effect of inlining its body at the single call site. Out-of-tree callers (extensions/custom providers) referencing this method fail at compile time on upgrade with no deprecation cycle.

[ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() loads and evaluates permissions for every group resource in the realm via resourceStore.findByType on each user-search request. Realms with many group-scoped permissions pay a per-request O(groups) policy-evaluation cost on the user search path that previously was served by the V1 path's direct policy lookup, degrading list-users latency for restricted admins.

[ADVISORY] canList() was reordered from `canView() || hasOneAdminRole(...)` to `hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()` in the same PR, a semantic-neutral-looking shuffle that changes evaluation order and is not required by the Groups-scope feature. The next reader must re-verify whether the reordering was intentional (it now short-circuits on QUERY_GROUPS before the V2 override's more expensive evaluation), adding review burden unrelated to the feature.

[ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2 overrides 9 GroupPermissionManagement methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, viewPermission, managePermission, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission) to throw UnsupportedOperationException, meaning the V2 evaluator implements the manager interface with half its surface inert. Any admin endpoint or code path invoking group permission management while the V2 class is active fails at runtime with UnsupportedOperationException instead of a 4xx, and the invariant 'managers can report/configure their own permissions' is not enforced in the V2 path.

[BUG] The per-user usersEvaluator::canView filter is removed from searchForUser, so authorization is enforced only by the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, which is set only when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns a non-empty set. When the caller lacks view permission and the granted-group set is empty (cross-realm admin with !isAdminSameRealm, null realm resource server, or simply no group permissions), the old code filtered every user out via usersEvaluator::canView while the new code returns the raw searchForUserStream unfiltered — unauthorized admins get the full user list instead of an empty/forbidden result. The identical regression exists in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser (rest/admin-ui-ext/.../BruteForceUsersResource.java lines 144-156), which had the same filter removed.

[BUG] Same removal of the usersEvaluator::canView filter as UsersResource: brute-force user search now returns the unfiltered search stream whenever the group-restriction attribute is not set. An admin without user-view permission and with no granted groups (e.g. isAdminSameRealm false or no realm permissions client) gets the complete user list from the brute-force detection endpoint instead of the previously filtered result.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage when the caller has only the VIEW scope on all-groups (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), contradicting canManage(GroupModel) which correctly requires only MANAGE. An admin granted view-only permission over groups passes canManage() and can perform management operations that gate on it (e.g. group creation, which the diff's own test asserts must require the manage scope), breaking the privilege separation the resource-type schema defines.

[BUG] Under the V2 evaluator, GroupPermissionManager mutators (setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, managePermission, etc.) throw UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener's group-removed event handler calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false). With the V2 feature enabled, deleting any group with permissions enabled reaches the listener and throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the event dispatch, turning group deletion into a failed operation (500) instead of a normal cleanup.

[ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() loads every group resource via resourceStore.findByType and runs a full hasPermission evaluation (resource lookup, policy lookup, evaluatePermission) per group on the user-search hot path, and duplicates the scope logic already maintained in the base GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. Realms with many groups pay O(n) authorization evaluations (each multiple DB queries) for every user search/list request by restricted admins; and when the scope set is later adjusted in one copy (as this diff already did for canViewMembers adding MANAGE_MEMBERS), the V1/V2 pair silently drifts.

[ADVISORY] GroupPermissions' private final fields (root, resourceStore, policyStore) are widened to protected solely so GroupPermissionsV2 can subclass and reuse V1 internals rather than share a common implementation. V2 is now coupled to V1's internal storage layout; any refactor of V1's stores breaks V2, and the V1/V2 split grows into two parallel permission implementations that must be kept behaviorally in sync by hand (already visible in canViewMembers/canManageMembers scope lists).

[BUG] The per-user permission filter (usersEvaluator::canView) was silently removed from searchForUser, so result filtering now relies solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute restricting the storage query. Any user record returned by searchForUserStream that is not excluded by the GROUPS attribute (e.g. users not belonging to any of the permitted groups, or storage providers that ignore the attribute) is now returned to callers who lack view permission on them — an authorization bypass on the user-search path, with no test in the diff covering this relaxed path.

[BUG] Same silent filter removal as UsersResource: the usersEvaluator::canView filter was dropped and the stream is returned directly from searchForUserStream. Brute-force user listings can include users the admin has no view permission for whenever the UserModel.GROUPS attribute does not fully constrain the underlying query; no test in the diff exercises this endpoint's permission behavior after the change.

[BUG] canMapRoles was silently tightened: it previously granted via canManage(user) (user-level MANAGE permission), and now only grants via raw MANAGE_USERS role, MAP_ROLES permission, or group manage-membership. Existing V2 deployments where an admin was granted user-level MANAGE permission lose the ability to map roles on those users without any migration or human-accepted decision recorded; the accompanying test diff contains no coverage of this narrowed grant.

[BUG] canManageGroupMembership was silently tightened the same way as canMapRoles: the previous canManage(user) shortcut was replaced with an explicit scope list, dropping user-level MANAGE as a sufficient grant for membership management. Admins holding user-level MANAGE permission in V2 can no longer manage group membership of those users unless the permission also carries MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP or a group MANAGE_MEMBERS grant — a regression of previously accepted behavior with no test asserting the new restriction.

[BUG] The AdminRoles.ADMIN fallback was silently removed from canView(UserModel) and canManage(UserModel), so realm masters/admins with only the ADMIN role no longer satisfy these checks via role membership. Callers relying on the pre-existing ADMIN-role shortcut in V2 lose per-user view/manage access after this change; the behavior delta is not reflected in any test or changelog entry in the diff.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage on the all-groups resource when only the VIEW (or MANAGE) scope is granted, meaning a view-only group permission elevates to manage. A principal granted just VIEW on all-groups passes canManage(), allowing group creation/update/child-add operations that the permission model intends to gate behind MANAGE — privilege escalation introduced without an accepted decision or a test asserting view-does-not-imply-manage.

[BUG] requireViewMembers was silently re-pointed from getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) to canViewMembers(group), and canViewMembers was simultaneously widened to accept MANAGE_MEMBERS in addition to VIEW_MEMBERS. Endpoints that previously required only VIEW_MEMBERS to view group members now also admit MANAGE_MEMBERS holders (a grant widening), and callers invoking requireViewMembers get a different permission decision than before — an objective change to the members-visibility contract made inside this diff without explicit acceptance.

[ADVISORY] canList() operand order was flipped (hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()) alongside a redefinition of canView() in the same diff, so the net permission set change is not verifiable by reading either hunk alone. Reviewers and future maintainers cannot determine from this diff whether query-groups-only admins gained or lost listing ability relative to the previous V1 semantics; reordering plus redefinition in one commit obscures the intent trail for an authorization decision.

[BUG] The per-user authorization filter (usersEvaluator::canView) was removed from searchForUser, so when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set the session GROUPS attribute is not set and searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm with no per-user authorization check. A caller holding only AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS (or only a fine-grained manage-users / user-level view permission, i.e. usersEvaluator.canView() false but no group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants) previously got an empty result from this endpoint because every user was filtered out; now the raw search runs unscoped and the endpoint returns the full user list (usernames, emails, attributes) of the realm — an authorization over-exposure / IDOR introduced by relying solely on the DB-level group scoping attribute.

[BUG] Same defect as UsersResource.searchForUser: the endpoint now depends entirely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute for scoping, and when groupIds is empty the brute-force user search runs completely unscoped with no per-user permission filter. A query-only admin (QUERY_USERS, no VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS and no group-level grants) calling the brute-force user listing receives all users of the realm, whereas the previous behavior (attribute set only when !auth.users().canView(), combined with the group-restricted store query) exposed nothing outside the granted groups.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as satisfying a manage check: hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) returns true if either scope is granted, unlike canManage(GroupModel) which requires only MANAGE. An admin granted only the all-groups 'view' permission (no manage anywhere) passes requireManage()/canManage(), so they can create groups (GroupsResource.add goes through auth.groups().requireManage()) — a view-only principal obtains a manage capability, a privilege over-grant in the new V2 evaluator.

[ADVISORY] The pre-permission assertion 'assertTrue(search.isEmpty())' asserts the whole user list is empty rather than that Alice is hidden, conflating 'cannot see Alice' with 'sees nothing', so the test's setup guarantee is weaker than the behavior it claims to establish. If any other realm user exists (e.g., a user created by the test framework or a prior test in the same realm when the suite is reordered), the setup assertion fails spuriously, or worse, if the realm gains a user between runs the test passes the setup check but the final assertEquals(1, search.size()) depends on total realm population, making the permission verdict indistinguishable from a population artifact.

[ADVISORY] The diff changes per-group list filtering (canViewGlobal || canView(g) replaced by unconditionally calling canView(g), whose V2 implementation now evaluates resource-level VIEW/MANAGE permissions per group), and no test in this diff exercises partial-visibility listing — the only new test file, GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, covers manage/view of a single known group and user search, never asserting that GET /groups returns only the groups the caller can view. A regression in GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) or in the stream filter (e.g., returning all groups, or zero groups) ships undetected; the caller most bitten is an admin with scoped group permissions who relies on the list endpoint for the admin console tree.

[ADVISORY] BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser is rewired to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission with the canView gate removed, and I checked the only test file in the diff (tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java) — no test references the brute-force endpoint, so the changed scoped-visibility behavior of that resource is entirely unverified. A regression where the brute-force user search either leaks all users or returns none for a scoped admin ships silently; operators of the admin UI brute-force page are the ones bitten, and nothing in the diff would catch it.

[ADVISORY] canList() is reordered from canView() || hasOneAdminRole(...) to hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView(), a semantic change (a VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS admin without group permissions now depends on the V2 hasPermission path differently), yet no test in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java or anywhere in the diff asserts group-listing permission for any of these role combinations. A caller with only query-groups, or a caller with view-users but no group permissions, gets list behavior that nothing verifies; a regression here surfaces as the admin console groups list either 403-ing or emptying for existing deployments, discovered only in production.

[BUG] No data migration/backfill exists in this diff to stamp existing fine-grained group permission resources with the new 'Groups' resource type, so GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)) and hasPermission (resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)) find nothing for any resource created by the pre-upgrade V1 code, which stored group resources under the name 'group.resource.<id>' with no resource type. After an upgrade of an existing realm using V1 fine-grained group permissions, every previously-granted group/view-members permission silently stops matching: administrators who had scoped access lose it (or, in the searchForUser path, the empty granted set means user results are filtered out), with no error indicating the persisted authorization data was not migrated — the stored permission data becomes orphaned and the outage is silent rather than a hard failure.

[ADVISORY] AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource now resolves group resources by bare group ID as the resource name, but any legacy resource for the same group persisted under the V1 name 'group.resource.<id>' is not matched, so a fresh duplicate resource is created for the same group instead of adopting the existing one. Upgraded realms accumulate duplicate authorization resources per group (old 'group.resource.<id>' resource with its policies plus a new bare-ID resource with none); existing policies remain attached to the orphaned legacy resource and never apply to the resource the V2 evaluator queries, and the leftover rows are never cleaned up by any step in this diff.

[BUG] searchForUser now returns ALL users to callers with no view permission and no group-scoped grants, because the per-user filter usersEvaluator::canView was removed and the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute is only set when the granted set is non-empty. An admin holding only QUERY_USERS (canQuery passes, canView() false) or a fine-grained admin whose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is empty previously got an empty result stream (the canView filter rejected every user); now with no attribute set and no filter, session.users().searchForUserStream searches across all users and the full realm user list is returned — a silent authorization over-share on the user search endpoint.

[BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage capability when the caller holds only a VIEW permission on all-groups, because it passes both AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW and AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE as acceptable scopes. An administrator granted only 'view' on the all-groups resource passes hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) and canManage() returns true, allowing group creation/deletion (requireManage passes) that the documented contract ('permission to MANAGE groups') restricts to MANAGE — a silent privilege over-grant compared to the V1 implementation, which required only the MANAGE_USERS admin role.

[ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in V2 iterates every group resource of the type and runs a full permission evaluation per group, and this is invoked unconditionally on every users search and brute-force user search request. Realms with a large number of fine-grained group permissions pay an O(N) authorization evaluation per user-search request (UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser both call it on the hot listing path); admins doing routine user listing see latency grow linearly with the number of group resources.

[BUG] getOrCreateResource throws a raw IllegalStateException for an unrecognized resourceType, surfacing as a 500 response where the caller-supplied input warrants a 4xx. A request path that reaches getOrCreateResource with a resourceType not in the schema (e.g. a stale or mistyped type identifier passed through the permissions API) produces an unhandled IllegalStateException → HTTP 500 with a stack trace path instead of a 400/404 the contract implies; the old if/else chain silently fell through with name=null, so this also converts previously tolerated inputs into hard failures.

[ADVISORY] hasPermission looks up per-group resources by resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) using the raw group id as the resource name, with no verification that the found resource is of the Groups type. If any resource in the realm resource server happens to be named with a group id (e.g. a user resource or legacy V1 resource under a different naming scheme like 'group.resource.<id>'), the check evaluates the wrong resource's scopes and returns a permission decision for the wrong entity — a silently wrong authorization answer rather than a 'not found' failure; also the mismatch with V1 naming (group.resource.<id> prefix) means V1-created group resources are silently not found by this lookup.

[ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in V1 now returns an empty (unrestricted-permission) set only for callers where root.users().canView() is true, dropping the previous root.users().canManage() bypass, so manage-only admins get group-restricted search semantics. An admin with MANAGE_USERS but not VIEW_USERS who previously got unfiltered user/group search results (empty set meant no session attribute restriction) is now silently scoped to group-granted results only; combined with the removed per-user filter in UsersResource.searchForUser, if their granted set is empty the search silently widens instead — the two changes interact to produce results that are neither the old filtered set nor the old full set.

goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s first claim is incorrect: the new `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest` *does* exercise `MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP` via `testManageGroupMembership()`, which grants `createGroupPermission(topGroup, Set.of(MANAGE_MEMBERSHIP), ...)` and then successfully calls `joinGroup(...)`. However, the second claim is diff-grounded: `UsersResource.searchForUser()` removed the explicit per-user visibility filter (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now relies on setting `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` from `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`; the new tests don’t include an “ungrouped user remains hidden” regression check after granting some group member-view permissions. That is a specific, nontrivial missing test for the behavioral/security-sensitive change in `UsersResource.java` around lines ~446-453.
