adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new fallback logic in `GroupPermissionsV2#hasPermission`: when `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` returns null, it evaluates permissions against the GROUPS *type* resource (`AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA.getResourceTypeResource(...)`), with only a guard `if (policyStore.findByResource(server, resource).isEmpty()) return false;`. The added tests (e.g., `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest#testManageAllGroups`) exercise the fallback only in the “all-groups permission exists” case, but there is no dedicated test asserting the guard blocks access when the type resource exists without policies. That’s a concrete, diff-grounded missing coverage for newly added, security-relevant decision logic, not a proven defect in the implementation as shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GroupPermissions.canList() was changed from canView()-first to QUERY_GROUPS-first and canManage()/canView() changed from users().canManageDefault()/canViewDefault() to direct role checks, while V1's getGroupsWithViewPermission lost its canManage() shortcut (now only root.users().canView()) — several subtle authorization-behavior changes bundled without any V1-path test updates in the visible diff. Existing fine-grained-authz deployments on the V1 path get silently altered evaluation order and manage-only admin behavior (e.g., a manage-users-only admin querying group lists now depends on canView() semantics that changed) with no regression coverage pinning the old contract.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does bundle multiple authorization logic changes in the V1 implementation without any clearly corresponding V1 regression tests in the shown changes: e.g., GroupPermissions.canList() changed from `canView() || root.hasOneAdminRole(...QUERY_GROUPS...)` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()`; GroupPermissions.canManage()/canView() switched to direct `root.hasOneAdminRole(...)` checks; `getGroupsWithViewPermission(GroupModel)` was removed and member-view checks were rewired (`requireViewMembers` now calls `canViewMembers`, and `canViewMembers` now accepts VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS). Although part of the finding overstates the impact (the removed `canManage()` shortcut in getGroupIdsWithViewPermission is likely redundant because `root.users().canView()` generally covers manage as well), the review concern about unpinned behavioral changes in the V1 path and lack of targeted regression coverage is specific and grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public static utility ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes is deleted while the diff only redirects its single in-tree caller, leaving any out-of-tree caller of the spi-private API with a compile break instead of a deprecation. Downstream extensions calling ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes fail to compile against this change; a @Deprecated forwarding stub would have preserved the public surface.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes the public static method `ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` from `server-spi-private` (see deletion in `ModelToRepresentation.java`) and updates the only in-tree caller (`GroupsResource`) to call `session.groups().searchGroupsByAttributes(...)` directly. That means any external/downstream code that previously called this public method will no longer compile. This is an API compatibility concern (compile-time break) rather than a runtime correctness defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The diff removes the `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` post-filter from searchForUser (and the equivalent structure in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser), replacing an in-stream authorization filter with only the UserModel.GROUPS session-attribute restriction — a behavior change not traceable to 'add Groups resource type and scopes'. When getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set for a caller who lacks global view but the underlying user storage provider ignores the session attribute (e.g. federated/custom UserQueryProvider implementations that do not honor UserModel.GROUPS), unauthorized users are returned where the previous code guaranteed filtering; also callers with canView()==true but restricted group visibility via fine-grained user permissions lose the per-user canView check entirely.

adjudication.rationale: The diff *does* remove an explicit authorization gate in `UsersResource.searchForUser`: it previously did `searchForUserStream(...).filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now passes the raw stream into `toRepresentation(...)` without that filter. That is a concrete, diff-grounded behavior change and raises a legitimate concern that authorization is now relying on the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute / storage-layer enforcement. However, the finding’s claim about an “equivalent” removed filter in `BruteForceUsersResource` is not supported by the diff (there was no `usersEvaluator::canView` filter there before), and whether unauthorized users are actually returned cannot be verified from this diff alone because `toRepresentation(...)` (not shown/changed here) may still enforce per-user visibility.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() returns true when the caller holds only a VIEW permission on all-groups, because it evaluates hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE). An admin granted only view-groups can create groups and perform manage-scope operations (e.g. GroupsResource.add, which requires canManage), a privilege escalation inconsistent with canManage(group) which correctly requires only MANAGE.
matched_golden_ids: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate describes the same bug: GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() incorrectly allows VIEW-only permission via hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE), enabling privilege escalation. It contrasts with canView() / canManage(group) behavior and states canManage should require MANAGE only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The V1 GroupPermissions.canManage()/canView() were rewritten from `root.users().canManageDefault()/canViewDefault()` to direct hasOneAdminRole checks, dropping the indirect dependency on fine-grained user permissions that users().canView()/canManage() previously included. In the V1 (non-V2) path, a caller who previously satisfied group view/manage via fine-grained user-level permissions (users().canView() includes the view-users authorization permission, not just admin roles) now loses group visibility — a silent permission regression unrelated to the stated goal of adding the Groups resource type.

adjudication.rationale: In the V1 path, GroupPermissions.canManage()/canView() previously called root.users().canManageDefault()/canViewDefault(), but those methods (removed in this diff) only checked admin roles (UserPermissions.canManageDefault(): root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS); canViewDefault(): root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS, VIEW_USERS)). They did not incorporate fine-grained user permissions like users().canView()/canManage(). The new direct hasOneAdminRole checks in GroupPermissions are equivalent to the removed *Default() methods, so the claimed permission regression is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The rewrite of ApiUtil.handleCreatedResponse to try-with-resources is unrelated refactoring bundled into a PR whose stated intent is adding the Groups resource type and scopes. Reviewers and bisect operate on a mixed-intent diff; if the response-close change regresses (e.g. getResponse read-after-close), it will be attributed to the authz change.

adjudication.rationale: The diff includes a behavioral-neutral refactor in `test-framework/core/.../ApiUtil.java` changing `handleCreatedResponse` from manual `response.close()` to `try (response) { ... }`. This change is orthogonal to the main functional changes around adding `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE` and related permission evaluation (e.g., `AdminPermissionsSchema`, `GroupPermissionsV2`, filtering changes in `GroupsResource`/`GroupResource`). While not a verifiable bug (the old code also closed the response before returning), it does mix an unrelated cleanup into a large authz-focused diff, which can hinder review/bisect if any test-client behavior changes are later suspected.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The public utility ModelToRepresentation.searchGroupModelsByAttributes is deleted outright rather than deprecated, removing a public API surface as a side effect of inlining its body at the single call site. Out-of-tree callers (extensions/custom providers) referencing this method fail at compile time on upgrade with no deprecation cycle.

adjudication.rationale: The diff removes `public static Stream<GroupModel> searchGroupModelsByAttributes(...)` from `ModelToRepresentation` entirely (lines deleted in `server-spi-private/src/main/java/org/keycloak/models/utils/ModelToRepresentation.java`), and replaces its only in-tree usage in `GroupsResource` with a direct call to `session.groups().searchGroupsByAttributes(...)`. This is a concrete API surface removal (compile-time breaking for any out-of-tree callers) rather than a functional/runtime defect, and there is no deprecation shim or replacement method left behind in `ModelToRepresentation`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() loads and evaluates permissions for every group resource in the realm via resourceStore.findByType on each user-search request. Realms with many group-scoped permissions pay a per-request O(groups) policy-evaluation cost on the user search path that previously was served by the V1 path's direct policy lookup, degrading list-users latency for restricted admins.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission(), which iterates over all group resources via resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...) and for each calls hasPermission(...), which performs root.evaluatePermission(...) (policy evaluation). UsersResource.searchForUser() (and BruteForceUsersResource) now calls auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() on the user search path and sets it into session when non-empty. This creates a clear per-request O(number of group resources) permission-evaluation cost for restricted admins. It’s a performance/latency concern grounded in the new code, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canList() was reordered from `canView() || hasOneAdminRole(...)` to `hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()` in the same PR, a semantic-neutral-looking shuffle that changes evaluation order and is not required by the Groups-scope feature. The next reader must re-verify whether the reordering was intentional (it now short-circuits on QUERY_GROUPS before the V2 override's more expensive evaluation), adding review burden unrelated to the feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupPermissions.canList()` from `canView() || root.hasOneAdminRole(...)` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()`, but this is not merely a “semantic-neutral-looking shuffle”: it also removes redundant role checks (since `canView()` already covers `MANAGE_USERS`/`VIEW_USERS` in both V1 and V2). The new order plausibly reduces work by avoiding the potentially expensive `canView()` evaluation when `QUERY_GROUPS` is present; nothing in the diff indicates this is unintended or problematic behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GroupPermissionsV2 overrides 9 GroupPermissionManagement methods (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, resource, getPermissions, viewPermission, managePermission, viewMembersPermission, manageMembersPermission, manageMembershipPermission) to throw UnsupportedOperationException, meaning the V2 evaluator implements the manager interface with half its surface inert. Any admin endpoint or code path invoking group permission management while the V2 class is active fails at runtime with UnsupportedOperationException instead of a 4xx, and the invariant 'managers can report/configure their own permissions' is not enforced in the V2 path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows `GroupPermissionsV2` extends `GroupPermissions` (which implements both `GroupPermissionEvaluator` and `GroupPermissionManagement`) but overrides multiple management methods (`isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `viewMembersPermission`, `manageMembersPermission`, `manageMembershipPermission`, `viewPermission`, `managePermission`, `resource`, `getPermissions`) to throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. Also, `MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()` now returns this `GroupPermissionsV2`, so any V2 code path that treats `groups()` as a management surface could crash. However, from this diff alone we cannot confirm that an admin endpoint/code path will actually invoke these management methods while V2 is active, so the runtime-failure claim is not fully verifiable as an introduced defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The per-user usersEvaluator::canView filter is removed from searchForUser, so authorization is enforced only by the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute, which is set only when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns a non-empty set. When the caller lacks view permission and the granted-group set is empty (cross-realm admin with !isAdminSameRealm, null realm resource server, or simply no group permissions), the old code filtered every user out via usersEvaluator::canView while the new code returns the raw searchForUserStream unfiltered — unauthorized admins get the full user list instead of an empty/forbidden result. The identical regression exists in BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser (rest/admin-ui-ext/.../BruteForceUsersResource.java lines 144-156), which had the same filter removed.

adjudication.rationale: In both `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the explicit per-user authorization filter (`.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`) and now always returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly. The only remaining restriction mechanism in these methods is setting `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)`, but that happens only when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. From the diff, `GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns `Collections.emptySet()` in multiple “no access” situations (e.g., `!root.isAdminSameRealm()`, `server == null`, or simply no group permissions found), meaning the session attribute will not be set and the user search stream is left unfiltered by `usersEvaluator`. Given that `UserPermissions.canQuery()` allows querying with `QUERY_USERS` even when `canView()` is false (diff shows `return root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS) || canView();`), this change can expose user listings to callers who can query but cannot view users, which is a security/correctness regression relative to the previous explicit filter.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Same removal of the usersEvaluator::canView filter as UsersResource: brute-force user search now returns the unfiltered search stream whenever the group-restriction attribute is not set. An admin without user-view permission and with no granted groups (e.g. isAdminSameRealm false or no realm permissions client) gets the complete user list from the brute-force detection endpoint instead of the previously filtered result.

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(), the diff does not remove any `usersEvaluator::canView` filter—there was no such filter in that method before (it already passed the raw `searchForUserStream(...)` into `toRepresentation(...)`). The only behavioral change shown is replacing `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` with `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and removing the `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard before setting the `UserModel.GROUPS` session attribute. The finding’s claim of a newly introduced unfiltered stream/complete user list leak due to “same removal … as UsersResource” is not verifiable from this file’s before/after state in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage when the caller has only the VIEW scope on all-groups (hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)), contradicting canManage(GroupModel) which correctly requires only MANAGE. An admin granted view-only permission over groups passes canManage() and can perform management operations that gate on it (e.g. group creation, which the diff's own test asserts must require the manage scope), breaking the privilege separation the resource-type schema defines.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`, the implementation returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, meaning a caller with only the VIEW scope on the all-groups (resource-type) permission will be treated as able to "manage" groups. This is inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel)` (which correctly checks only `MANAGE`) and with the privilege separation implied by the schema/tests (e.g., `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testManageAllGroups` comments that group creation requires MANAGE). The diff shows the logic clearly and it would allow escalation wherever management operations gate on `canManage()`/`requireManage()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Under the V2 evaluator, GroupPermissionManager mutators (setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, managePermission, etc.) throw UnsupportedOperationException, but AdminPermissions.registerListener's group-removed event handler calls management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false). With the V2 feature enabled, deleting any group with permissions enabled reaches the listener and throws UnsupportedOperationException inside the event dispatch, turning group deletion into a failed operation (500) instead of a normal cleanup.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces GroupPermissionsV2 (used by MgmtPermissionsV2.groups()) where GroupPermissionManagement mutators like setPermissionsEnabled(...) explicitly throw UnsupportedOperationException ("Not supported in V2"). However, AdminPermissions.registerListener (now only registered when ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ is enabled) still handles GroupRemovedEvent by calling management(...).groups().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getGroup(), false) with no guard/try-catch. If management(...) resolves to MgmtPermissionsV2 under the enabled feature, this call will throw during event dispatch, potentially breaking group deletion/cleanup.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() loads every group resource via resourceStore.findByType and runs a full hasPermission evaluation (resource lookup, policy lookup, evaluatePermission) per group on the user-search hot path, and duplicates the scope logic already maintained in the base GroupPermissions.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission. Realms with many groups pay O(n) authorization evaluations (each multiple DB queries) for every user search/list request by restricted admins; and when the scope set is later adjusted in one copy (as this diff already did for canViewMembers adding MANAGE_MEMBERS), the V1/V2 pair silently drifts.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds/uses `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` which iterates all group resources via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each calls `hasPermission(...)`, which itself may do `resourceStore.findByName(...)`, `policyStore.findByResource(...)`, and `root.evaluatePermission(...)` (see new file `GroupPermissionsV2.java`). The user search/count paths now call `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` (e.g., `UsersResource.searchForUser` and `getUsersCount`, and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser`), so restricted admins can trigger this per request, making the O(n) per-group auth evaluation concern diff-grounded. The V2 method also hard-codes scope sets (`VIEW_MEMBERS`, `MANAGE_MEMBERS`) duplicating similar logic in the V1 `GroupPermissions` implementation, creating a realistic drift/maintenance risk when scope logic changes (as seen elsewhere in the diff adjusting view-members behavior to include `MANAGE_MEMBERS`). This is a performance/architecture issue rather than a directly verifiable functional bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] GroupPermissions' private final fields (root, resourceStore, policyStore) are widened to protected solely so GroupPermissionsV2 can subclass and reuse V1 internals rather than share a common implementation. V2 is now coupled to V1's internal storage layout; any refactor of V1's stores breaks V2, and the V1/V2 split grows into two parallel permission implementations that must be kept behaviorally in sync by hand (already visible in canViewMembers/canManageMembers scope lists).

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly widens `GroupPermissions` internals from `private final` to `protected final` (`root`, `resourceStore`, `policyStore`) and then introduces `GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions`, which directly relies on those inherited fields (e.g., `root...`, `resourceStore.findByType(...)`, `policyStore.findByResource(...)`). This creates tight coupling between V2 and V1’s internal storage/layout and encourages parallel, duplicated permission logic across V1/V2 (many overridden methods in `GroupPermissionsV2` re-implement checks). This is a concrete, diff-grounded maintainability/architecture concern rather than an immediately verifiable functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The per-user permission filter (usersEvaluator::canView) was silently removed from searchForUser, so result filtering now relies solely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute restricting the storage query. Any user record returned by searchForUserStream that is not excluded by the GROUPS attribute (e.g. users not belonging to any of the permitted groups, or storage providers that ignore the attribute) is now returned to callers who lack view permission on them — an authorization bypass on the user-search path, with no test in the diff covering this relaxed path.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` the stream `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` is no longer filtered with `usersEvaluator::canView` (removed: `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)`). The only remaining restriction is the optional `session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds)` based on `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()`, but this attribute is only set when that set is non-empty. If `groupIds` is empty (e.g., a caller can query but has no group view-members grants), the query runs without the previous per-user authorization filter, and the method returns representations for whatever the storage returns. The same pattern appears in `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)` (filter removal / reliance on GROUPS attribute). This is a concrete authorization-relaxing change visible in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Same silent filter removal as UsersResource: the usersEvaluator::canView filter was dropped and the stream is returned directly from searchForUserStream. Brute-force user listings can include users the admin has no view permission for whenever the UserModel.GROUPS attribute does not fully constrain the underlying query; no test in the diff exercises this endpoint's permission behavior after the change.

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource#searchForUser (and the analogous method in UsersResource), the diff does not show any `usersEvaluator::canView` filter being removed from the brute-force endpoint: previously it did `Stream<UserModel> userModels = session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` and returned `toRepresentation(...)` without filtering, and after the change it still returns `toRepresentation(..., session.users().searchForUserStream(...))` without any filter. The only functional change here is switching from `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and removing the `if (!auth.users().canView())` wrapper, but `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is documented/implemented to return an empty set when the caller can view users, making the wrapper redundant. Therefore the finding’s claim of a “silent filter removal” in the brute-force listing is not supported by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canMapRoles was silently tightened: it previously granted via canManage(user) (user-level MANAGE permission), and now only grants via raw MANAGE_USERS role, MAP_ROLES permission, or group manage-membership. Existing V2 deployments where an admin was granted user-level MANAGE permission lose the ability to map roles on those users without any migration or human-accepted decision recorded; the accompanying test diff contains no coverage of this narrowed grant.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does not show a tightening that removes user-level MANAGE from granting role-mapping. In `UserPermissionsV2.canMapRoles`, the new logic explicitly calls `hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES) || canManageByGroup(user)`. Because `hasPermission(...)` returns true if *any* granted scope matches the expected list, a user-level `MANAGE` permission alone still satisfies `canMapRoles` (since `MANAGE` is included in the expected scopes). So V2 deployments with user-level MANAGE permission would not lose `canMapRoles` due to this change, contrary to the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] canManageGroupMembership was silently tightened the same way as canMapRoles: the previous canManage(user) shortcut was replaced with an explicit scope list, dropping user-level MANAGE as a sufficient grant for membership management. Admins holding user-level MANAGE permission in V2 can no longer manage group membership of those users unless the permission also carries MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP or a group MANAGE_MEMBERS grant — a regression of previously accepted behavior with no test asserting the new restriction.

adjudication.rationale: In `UserPermissionsV2.canManageGroupMembership`, the change does not drop user-level `MANAGE` as a sufficient grant. The new code explicitly checks `hasPermission(user, null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_GROUP_MEMBERSHIP) || canManageByGroup(user)`, so a permission carrying `MANAGE` still returns true. Previously it short-circuited via `canManage(user)`, which itself is `hasPermission(...MANAGE) || canManageByGroup(user)`. This is not a tightening/regression as described; it preserves `MANAGE` and group-based grants.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The AdminRoles.ADMIN fallback was silently removed from canView(UserModel) and canManage(UserModel), so realm masters/admins with only the ADMIN role no longer satisfy these checks via role membership. Callers relying on the pre-existing ADMIN-role shortcut in V2 lose per-user view/manage access after this change; the behavior delta is not reflected in any test or changelog entry in the diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly removes `AdminRoles.ADMIN` from the role-based short-circuit checks in `UserPermissionsV2`: `canView(UserModel user)` changes from `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)` to only `MANAGE_USERS, VIEW_USERS`, and `canManage(UserModel user)` changes from `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.ADMIN, AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS)` to only `MANAGE_USERS`. This is a concrete behavior change visible in the diff that can reduce access for principals that previously relied on the `ADMIN` role shortcut in V2 for per-user view/manage decisions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage on the all-groups resource when only the VIEW (or MANAGE) scope is granted, meaning a view-only group permission elevates to manage. A principal granted just VIEW on all-groups passes canManage(), allowing group creation/update/child-add operations that the permission model intends to gate behind MANAGE — privilege escalation introduced without an accepted decision or a test asserting view-does-not-imply-manage.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, i.e., it treats a VIEW grant on the global/all-groups resource as sufficient for “manage” capability. If any write operation is guarded by `auth.groups().requireManage()` / `canManage()` (e.g., group creation at `/groups`), then a principal with only VIEW on all-groups would be incorrectly authorized to perform manage actions. The accompanying tests distinguish VIEW vs MANAGE for all-groups (e.g., `testManageAllGroups()` uses `MANAGE` for creation), but there is no test asserting that VIEW does *not* permit manage, reinforcing that this is unintended privilege elevation.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] requireViewMembers was silently re-pointed from getGroupsWithViewPermission(group) to canViewMembers(group), and canViewMembers was simultaneously widened to accept MANAGE_MEMBERS in addition to VIEW_MEMBERS. Endpoints that previously required only VIEW_MEMBERS to view group members now also admit MANAGE_MEMBERS holders (a grant widening), and callers invoking requireViewMembers get a different permission decision than before — an objective change to the members-visibility contract made inside this diff without explicit acceptance.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `GroupPermissions.requireViewMembers` from using `getGroupsWithViewPermission(group)` to `canViewMembers(group)`, and it widens `canViewMembers` to accept `MANAGE_MEMBERS` in addition to `VIEW_MEMBERS` (`return hasPermission(group, VIEW_MEMBERS_SCOPE, MANAGE_MEMBERS_SCOPE);`). However, this is not “silent” or unaccepted in the diff: the `GroupPermissionEvaluator` interface Javadoc is updated to explicitly document that `canViewMembers` may be granted by `VIEW_MEMBERS` *or* `MANAGE_MEMBERS`, and a new test `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers` is added asserting that `MANAGE_MEMBERS` permits seeing the user. So the finding’s claim that this was done without explicit acceptance/made unintentionally is contradicted by the diff itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canList() operand order was flipped (hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()) alongside a redefinition of canView() in the same diff, so the net permission set change is not verifiable by reading either hunk alone. Reviewers and future maintainers cannot determine from this diff whether query-groups-only admins gained or lost listing ability relative to the previous V1 semantics; reordering plus redefinition in one commit obscures the intent trail for an authorization decision.

adjudication.rationale: In GroupPermissions.canList() the change from `canView() || root.hasOneAdminRole(..., QUERY_GROUPS)` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()` does not change the boolean result (no side effects shown in either operand). Also, query-groups-only admins are still explicitly granted listing via `hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.QUERY_GROUPS)`. The nearby canView() change in the same diff (from `root.users().canViewDefault()` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(MANAGE_USERS, VIEW_USERS)`) is effectively equivalent to the removed `canViewDefault()` implementation, so the alleged “net permission set change is not verifiable” is not supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The per-user authorization filter (usersEvaluator::canView) was removed from searchForUser, so when getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() returns an empty set the session GROUPS attribute is not set and searchForUserStream returns every user in the realm with no per-user authorization check. A caller holding only AdminRoles.QUERY_USERS (or only a fine-grained manage-users / user-level view permission, i.e. usersEvaluator.canView() false but no group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants) previously got an empty result from this endpoint because every user was filtered out; now the raw search runs unscoped and the endpoint returns the full user list (usernames, emails, attributes) of the realm — an authorization over-exposure / IDOR introduced by relying solely on the DB-level group scoping attribute.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` the stream-level authorization filter `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` was removed, and the only remaining restriction is setting `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` when `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is non-empty. If that method returns an empty set (e.g., caller can query users but has no group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS grants, and `root.users().canView()` is false), the code does not set `UserModel.GROUPS` and then returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` unfiltered. From the diff, no other per-user check is applied in this method anymore, so this change can expose users that `usersEvaluator.canView(user)` would have filtered out before.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] Same defect as UsersResource.searchForUser: the endpoint now depends entirely on the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute for scoping, and when groupIds is empty the brute-force user search runs completely unscoped with no per-user permission filter. A query-only admin (QUERY_USERS, no VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS and no group-level grants) calling the brute-force user listing receives all users of the realm, whereas the previous behavior (attribute set only when !auth.users().canView(), combined with the group-restricted store query) exposed nothing outside the granted groups.

adjudication.rationale: In BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser, the diff changes the permission helper used (getGroupsWithViewPermission -> getGroupIdsWithViewPermission) and removes the surrounding `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard, but the core behavior the finding complains about (not setting `UserModel.GROUPS` when the returned set is empty, and not applying a `usersEvaluator::canView` filter to the resulting stream) was already present in the pre-change code shown: previously it also only set the session attribute when the set was non-empty and then returned `toRepresentation(...)` over an unfiltered `searchForUserStream(...)`. Therefore the claim that this PR makes the endpoint “now” rely entirely on the session attribute / introduces a regression versus “previous behavior exposed nothing” is not supported by the diff. Also, whether a QUERY_USERS-only admin can call this endpoint and receive all users cannot be verified from the provided diff context (no enclosing auth checks shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() accepts the VIEW scope as satisfying a manage check: hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) returns true if either scope is granted, unlike canManage(GroupModel) which requires only MANAGE. An admin granted only the all-groups 'view' permission (no manage anywhere) passes requireManage()/canManage(), so they can create groups (GroupsResource.add goes through auth.groups().requireManage()) — a view-only principal obtains a manage capability, a privilege over-grant in the new V2 evaluator.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`, and `hasPermission(...)` returns true if *any* of the provided scopes is granted. That means an all-groups permission granting only `VIEW` would make `canManage()` true, unlike `canManage(GroupModel)` which correctly checks only `MANAGE`. Given group creation flows typically gate on `auth.groups().requireManage()` (as the finding notes), this is a privilege over-grant enabled by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The pre-permission assertion 'assertTrue(search.isEmpty())' asserts the whole user list is empty rather than that Alice is hidden, conflating 'cannot see Alice' with 'sees nothing', so the test's setup guarantee is weaker than the behavior it claims to establish. If any other realm user exists (e.g., a user created by the test framework or a prior test in the same realm when the suite is reordered), the setup assertion fails spuriously, or worse, if the realm gains a user between runs the test passes the setup check but the final assertEquals(1, search.size()) depends on total realm population, making the permission verdict indistinguishable from a population artifact.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`, the setup in `testCanViewUserByViewGroupMembers()` and `testCanViewUserByManageGroupMembers()` does `users().search(null, -1, -1)` followed by `assertTrue(search.isEmpty())` while the comment claims “my admin should NOT be able to see Alice”. This asserts the entire visible user list is empty, not specifically that Alice is absent, and later assertions (`assertEquals(1, search.size())`) similarly depend on total realm user population. That makes the test brittle/spurious if any other user becomes visible to `myadmin` (framework-created users, prior tests, or realm config changes).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff changes per-group list filtering (canViewGlobal || canView(g) replaced by unconditionally calling canView(g), whose V2 implementation now evaluates resource-level VIEW/MANAGE permissions per group), and no test in this diff exercises partial-visibility listing — the only new test file, GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java, covers manage/view of a single known group and user search, never asserting that GET /groups returns only the groups the caller can view. A regression in GroupPermissionsV2.canView(group) or in the stream filter (e.g., returning all groups, or zero groups) ships undetected; the caller most bitten is an admin with scoped group permissions who relies on the list endpoint for the admin console tree.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there is no test exercising partial-visibility listing of GET /groups after changing the stream filter to `.filter(groupsEvaluator::canView)`. However, the newly added `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.testViewGroups()` explicitly asserts that (1) the caller initially sees 0 groups, (2) after granting VIEW on a single specific group it sees exactly 1 group (only `myGroup`), and (3) after granting a realm-wide/all-groups VIEW permission it sees 2 groups. That directly tests partial visibility behavior of the list endpoint.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser is rewired to getGroupIdsWithViewPermission with the canView gate removed, and I checked the only test file in the diff (tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java) — no test references the brute-force endpoint, so the changed scoped-visibility behavior of that resource is entirely unverified. A regression where the brute-force user search either leaks all users or returns none for a scoped admin ships silently; operators of the admin UI brute-force page are the ones bitten, and nothing in the diff would catch it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser to always compute `groupIds = auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and set `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS` without the prior `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard. This is nontrivial authorization/scoping wiring for the brute-force admin UI endpoint (`rest/admin-ui-ext/.../BruteForceUsersResource.java`). The only newly added test in the diff (`GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest`) exercises group/user permission evaluation via the standard admin endpoints (users/groups), and nothing in the diff adds coverage for the brute-force resource’s search behavior. So the concern is actionable as a gap: the changed scoped-visibility logic for the brute-force user search is not directly tested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] canList() is reordered from canView() || hasOneAdminRole(...) to hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView(), a semantic change (a VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS admin without group permissions now depends on the V2 hasPermission path differently), yet no test in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java or anywhere in the diff asserts group-listing permission for any of these role combinations. A caller with only query-groups, or a caller with view-users but no group permissions, gets list behavior that nothing verifies; a regression here surfaces as the admin console groups list either 403-ing or emptying for existing deployments, discovered only in production.

adjudication.rationale: The change in GroupPermissions.canList() from `canView() || root.hasOneAdminRole(..., QUERY_GROUPS)` to `root.hasOneAdminRole(QUERY_GROUPS) || canView()` does not alter the boolean outcome because both operands are pure checks (no side effects shown in the diff), so reordering only affects short-circuit evaluation cost. In V2, `GroupPermissionsV2.canView()` still returns true immediately for `MANAGE_USERS/VIEW_USERS` roles before any `hasPermission(...)` evaluation, so a VIEW_USERS/MANAGE_USERS admin does not “depend on the V2 hasPermission path differently” as claimed. Also, the new `testViewGroups` in GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest exercises listing behavior for a user with `QUERY_GROUPS` (added in RealmAdminPermissionsConfig) and no group permissions, asserting the list is empty (not 403), contradicting the claim that nothing verifies this behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] No data migration/backfill exists in this diff to stamp existing fine-grained group permission resources with the new 'Groups' resource type, so GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission (resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)) and hasPermission (resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)) find nothing for any resource created by the pre-upgrade V1 code, which stored group resources under the name 'group.resource.<id>' with no resource type. After an upgrade of an existing realm using V1 fine-grained group permissions, every previously-granted group/view-members permission silently stops matching: administrators who had scoped access lose it (or, in the searchForUser path, the empty granted set means user results are filtered out), with no error indicating the persisted authorization data was not migrated — the stored permission data becomes orphaned and the outage is silent rather than a hard failure.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes how group permission resources are identified and discovered in V2: GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() looks up a group resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (raw group id), and getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() enumerates resources via `findByType(..., AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)`. Meanwhile, the existing GroupPermissions codebase clearly uses a different persisted naming scheme (`RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX = "group.resource."` and `getGroupResourceName(group)`), and AdminPermissionsSchema only now introduces a distinct `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. There is no compatibility lookup for the legacy `group.resource.<id>` names and no migration/backfill shown in the diff to re-stamp existing stored resources to the new name/type, so previously-created fine-grained group permissions are plausibly orphaned/ignored after upgrade.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource now resolves group resources by bare group ID as the resource name, but any legacy resource for the same group persisted under the V1 name 'group.resource.<id>' is not matched, so a fresh duplicate resource is created for the same group instead of adopting the existing one. Upgraded realms accumulate duplicate authorization resources per group (old 'group.resource.<id>' resource with its policies plus a new bare-ID resource with none); existing policies remain attached to the orphaned legacy resource and never apply to the resource the V2 evaluator queries, and the leftover rows are never cleaned up by any step in this diff.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows a concrete resource-name mismatch between the pre-existing group-permission model and the new V2 evaluation path. Legacy group resources in `GroupPermissions` are named with `RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX = "group.resource."` (see `getGroupResourceName(GroupModel)`), i.e. `group.resource.<groupId>`. New V2 logic in `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission(...)` looks up a group resource via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (bare ID), and `AdminPermissionsSchema` now resolves group resources to `group.getId()` via `resolveGroup(...)` and adds `GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`. There is no code in the diff that attempts to also look up/adopt the legacy `group.resource.<id>` resource name or migrate/clean up existing resources/policies. Therefore, on upgraded realms with existing group policies attached to legacy-named resources, V2 lookups will not find them and will behave as if no per-group policy exists (and can create new resources with the bare-id name elsewhere), leaving duplicates and orphaned policies.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] searchForUser now returns ALL users to callers with no view permission and no group-scoped grants, because the per-user filter usersEvaluator::canView was removed and the UserModel.GROUPS session attribute is only set when the granted set is non-empty. An admin holding only QUERY_USERS (canQuery passes, canView() false) or a fine-grained admin whose getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() is empty previously got an empty result stream (the canView filter rejected every user); now with no attribute set and no filter, session.users().searchForUserStream searches across all users and the full realm user list is returned — a silent authorization over-share on the user search endpoint.

adjudication.rationale: In `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)`, the diff removes the explicit authorization filter `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` and now always returns `session.users().searchForUserStream(...)` directly to `toRepresentation(...)`. The only remaining restriction attempt is setting `session` attribute `UserModel.GROUPS`, but this is done only when `groupIds` is non-empty (`if (!groupIds.isEmpty()) { session.setAttribute(UserModel.GROUPS, groupIds); }`). For callers where `usersEvaluator.canView()` is false and `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` returns an empty set, the session attribute is not set and no per-user filter is applied in this method, so the returned stream is no longer constrained by view permission. The diff does not show any compensating filter added in `toRepresentation(...)`, so the finding that this can over-share users via search is consistent with the changes shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] GroupPermissionsV2.canManage() grants manage capability when the caller holds only a VIEW permission on all-groups, because it passes both AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW and AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE as acceptable scopes. An administrator granted only 'view' on the all-groups resource passes hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE) and canManage() returns true, allowing group creation/deletion (requireManage passes) that the documented contract ('permission to MANAGE groups') restricts to MANAGE — a silent privilege over-grant compared to the V1 implementation, which required only the MANAGE_USERS admin role.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GroupPermissionsV2`, `canManage()` returns `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)` when the caller lacks `MANAGE_USERS` (see `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()`). The helper `hasPermission(null, ...)` explicitly falls back to the "all-groups" resource-type resource and returns true if *any* of the provided scopes is granted. Therefore, an admin granted only `VIEW` on the all-groups permission would satisfy `canManage()` and pass `requireManage()`, enabling manage-level operations gated by `requireManage()` (e.g., group creation) even without `MANAGE`. This is also internally inconsistent with `canManage(GroupModel)`, which requires `MANAGE` only.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in V2 iterates every group resource of the type and runs a full permission evaluation per group, and this is invoked unconditionally on every users search and brute-force user search request. Realms with a large number of fine-grained group permissions pay an O(N) authorization evaluation per user-search request (UsersResource.searchForUser, BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser both call it on the hot listing path); admins doing routine user listing see latency grow linearly with the number of group resources.

adjudication.rationale: The diff makes `UsersResource.searchForUser(...)` and `BruteForceUsersResource.searchForUser(...)` call `auth.groups().getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` on every request (the prior `if (!auth.users().canView())` guard was removed). In V2, `GroupPermissionsV2.getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` iterates all group resources via `resourceStore.findByType(..., GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` and for each calls `hasPermission(...)`, which runs `root.evaluatePermission(...)` (a full permission evaluation) per group. This creates an O(number-of-group-resources) authorization cost on the hot user-search/listing path for callers who cannot `root.users().canView()`, i.e., a concrete performance/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getOrCreateResource throws a raw IllegalStateException for an unrecognized resourceType, surfacing as a 500 response where the caller-supplied input warrants a 4xx. A request path that reaches getOrCreateResource with a resourceType not in the schema (e.g. a stale or mistyped type identifier passed through the permissions API) produces an unhandled IllegalStateException → HTTP 500 with a stack trace path instead of a 400/404 the contract implies; the old if/else chain silently fell through with name=null, so this also converts previously tolerated inputs into hard failures.

adjudication.rationale: In AdminPermissionsSchema#getOrCreateResource the diff replaces an if/else chain with a switch that has a `default -> throw new IllegalStateException("Resource type [" + resourceType + "] not found.")`. Previously, an unrecognized `resourceType` would leave `name` unset (null) and then follow the existing `if (name == null) { ... }` path rather than throwing. The diff therefore does introduce a hard failure for unknown types, but the claim that it "warrants a 4xx" and will "surface as 500" depends on how this method is called/handled elsewhere (not shown in the diff), so it’s an error-handling/behavior-change concern rather than a definitively verifiable bug from this diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] hasPermission looks up per-group resources by resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId) using the raw group id as the resource name, with no verification that the found resource is of the Groups type. If any resource in the realm resource server happens to be named with a group id (e.g. a user resource or legacy V1 resource under a different naming scheme like 'group.resource.<id>'), the check evaluates the wrong resource's scopes and returns a permission decision for the wrong entity — a silently wrong authorization answer rather than a 'not found' failure; also the mismatch with V1 naming (group.resource.<id> prefix) means V1-created group resources are silently not found by this lookup.

adjudication.rationale: In the new `GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission`, per-group resources are resolved via `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` (raw group id as the *resource name*) and then used without any verification of the resource's type (`AdminPermissionsSchema.GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE`). If any other resource in the same `ResourceServer` happens to have `name == groupId`, V2 will evaluate scopes against the wrong resource and return an authorization decision for the wrong entity. Additionally, existing (V1) per-group resources appear to be named with a prefix (`GroupPermissions` still contains `RESOURCE_NAME_PREFIX = "group.resource."` and `getGroupResourceName(group)`), so V1-created group resources would not be found by this V2 lookup, leading to silently missing per-group permissions rather than a clear not-found path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() in V1 now returns an empty (unrestricted-permission) set only for callers where root.users().canView() is true, dropping the previous root.users().canManage() bypass, so manage-only admins get group-restricted search semantics. An admin with MANAGE_USERS but not VIEW_USERS who previously got unfiltered user/group search results (empty set meant no session attribute restriction) is now silently scoped to group-granted results only; combined with the removed per-user filter in UsersResource.searchForUser, if their granted set is empty the search silently widens instead — the two changes interact to produce results that are neither the old filtered set nor the old full set.

adjudication.rationale: The finding’s core premise (“dropping the previous root.users().canManage() bypass, so MANAGE_USERS-only admins become group-restricted”) is not supported by the diff because `root.users().canView()` already encompasses MANAGE_USERS: `UserPermissions.canView()` returns true for `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_USERS, AdminRoles.VIEW_USERS)`. Therefore a MANAGE_USERS-but-not-VIEW_USERS admin still yields an empty set from `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and remains unrestricted, so the alleged behavioral regression for “manage-only admins” does not follow from the shown changes. While the per-user `.filter(usersEvaluator::canView)` was removed in `UsersResource.searchForUser`, the specific interaction described (manage-only scoping + empty-set widening) cannot be verified from the diff as written.
